title: Personal income tax in Mauritius
summary: How a person's income is taxed in Mauritius in the income year from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027: who is resident, the bands, the deductions for dependents, the other reliefs and their caps, what CSG and the National Savings Fund take from a salary, PAYE, and how a self-employed person pays. It is general information, not tax advice.
audience: Employees, pensioners and self-employed people who want to see how their income tax is worked out.

facts.label: Income year
facts.value: 1 July to 30 June
facts.detail: The figures here are for the income year from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027.

facts.label: Income tax bands
facts.value: 0% on the first MUR 500,000, 10% on the next MUR 500,000, 20% on the next MUR 11 million, 35% on the remainder
facts.detail: On chargeable income. Each rate applies only to its own slice. The 35% band is new from 1 July 2026.

facts.label: Deduction for dependents
facts.value: MUR 110,000 for one, MUR 190,000 for two, MUR 275,000 for three, MUR 355,000 for four or more
facts.detail: For a resident. A spouse, a child, or a bedridden next of kin in the person's care can be a dependent.

facts.label: Additional deduction, retired or disabled person
facts.detail: For a person aged 60 before the income year starts, with no business income and no pay above MUR 50,000, or a person with a disability.

facts.label: Additional deduction, child at university
facts.value: MUR 500,000 for each child, for up to 4 children
facts.detail: A dependent child on a full-time course that is not sponsored, for no more than 6 years.

facts.label: Additional deduction, private school fees
facts.value: The fees paid, up to MUR 60,000 for each child
facts.detail: A dependent child at a fee-paying private primary or secondary school.

facts.label: Relief for housing loan interest
facts.value: The interest paid, where income is MUR 4 million or less
facts.detail: The Act sets no cap in rupees. The loan must be secured on property and used only to buy or build the person's house.

facts.label: Relief for medical insurance
facts.value: Up to MUR 25,000 each for self and a first dependent, MUR 20,000 each for up to 3 more
facts.detail: The premium paid for the person and the dependents claimed. Not where the employer pays it.

facts.label: Deduction for a personal pension scheme
facts.value: The contribution, up to MUR 50,000
facts.detail: An individual pension scheme approved by the Financial Services Commission.

facts.label: Deduction for donations to charities
facts.value: The amount given, up to MUR 100,000
facts.detail: Given by electronic means to a charitable institution.

facts.label: Deduction for a carer's wages
facts.value: The wages paid, up to MUR 30,000
facts.detail: A carer employed for a parent or grandparent, with social contributions paid. The older deduction for household employees ended on 30 June 2025.

facts.label: Fair Share Contribution, individuals
facts.value: None for the income year from 1 July 2026
facts.detail: It was 15% of leviable income above MUR 12 million, for the income year that started on 1 July 2025 only.

facts.label: Reliefs for a non-resident
facts.value: None
facts.detail: Only a person resident in Mauritius in the income year can claim the deductions and reliefs. The bands are the same.

facts.label: CSG on a salary
facts.value: 1.5% where monthly basic pay is MUR 50,000 or less, 3% where it is more
facts.detail: The employee's share, on the whole basic wage or salary. An end of year bonus counts as a month of its own.

facts.label: National Savings Fund on a salary
facts.value: 1% of basic pay up to MUR 29,710 a month
facts.detail: The employee's share, from 1 July 2026. Not charged on a bonus.

facts.label: National Savings Fund, lowest wage charged
facts.value: MUR 4,580 a month
facts.detail: MUR 2,910 for a private household employee. From 1 July 2026.

facts.label: CSG for the self-employed
facts.value: MUR 150 a month where monthly net income is MUR 10,000 or less, 1.5% of 90% of it up to MUR 50,000, 3% of 90% of it above
facts.detail: Never less than MUR 150 a month. Income from rent, dividends and interest is left out.

facts.label: PAYE exemption
facts.value: MUR 38,462 a month
facts.detail: No tax is withheld from an employee whose emoluments in a month are at or below this. Directors' fees are an exception.

facts.label: Current Payment System threshold
facts.value: Gross income above MUR 4 million
facts.detail: A self-employed person files quarterly statements where last year's gross income from business and rent was above this.

facts.label: Individual return and payment
facts.value: By 15 October
facts.detail: After the income year ends on 30 June. Thursday 15 October 2026 for the year ended 30 June 2026.

blocks.text: A resident of Mauritius pays income tax on income from anywhere in the world. A non-resident pays on income from Mauritius. The income year runs from 1 July to 30 June. Tax is charged on chargeable income: gross income, less the deductions allowed in earning it, less the personal deductions and reliefs below.

The bands are progressive: each rate applies only to the slice of income inside its band. On a chargeable income of MUR 1.2 million, the first MUR 500,000 bears nothing, the next MUR 500,000 bears MUR 50,000 and the last MUR 200,000 bears MUR 40,000. The tax is MUR 90,000.

The 35% band is new. The Finance Act 2026 brought it in from 1 July 2026, on chargeable income above MUR 12 million. The year before, the top rate was 20% and a separate Fair Share Contribution took 15% of leviable income above MUR 12 million. That contribution ended for individuals after that one year. On 20 November 2026 the MRA's page on the obligation to file, its PAYE page and its tax calculator still showed the 2025-2026 bands. This article follows the Income Tax Act as consolidated up to the Finance Act 2026.

items: A person whose domicile is in Mauritius, unless their permanent place of abode is outside Mauritius.
A person present in Mauritius for 183 days or more in the income year.
A person present for 270 days or more in total over that income year and the two before it.

blocks.text: Only a resident can claim the deductions and reliefs. A non-resident's pay is taxed on the same bands with nothing taken off, and rent, royalties and other income from property at a flat 15%.
There is no longer an Income Exemption Threshold by category. Since 1 July 2023 a 0% band does that work for everyone, and a resident with dependents deducts a set amount for them.

items: A dependent is a spouse, a child under 18, an older child in full-time education or kept from earning by a disability, or a bedridden next of kin in the person's care.
Where one spouse claims for dependents, the other cannot.
No deduction is due for a dependent whose own income is above MUR 110,000 for the first, MUR 80,000 for the second, MUR 85,000 for the third or MUR 80,000 for the fourth.
A retired person, or a person with a disability, deducts a further MUR 50,000. Retired means aged 60 before the income year starts, with no business income and no pay above MUR 50,000.

rows: MUR 500,000 a child, up to 4 children
A full-time course, undergraduate or postgraduate, that is not sponsored. Not beyond 6 years, nor where tuition for an undergraduate course in Mauritius is under MUR 34,800
Dependent child at a fee-paying private school
The fees or MUR 60,000 a child, whichever is lower
A primary or secondary school registered under the Education Act
The interest paid. No cap in rupees
A loan secured on property, used only to buy or build the person's house. Not where the person or spouse already owned a residential building, or has income above MUR 4 million
MUR 25,000 each for self and a first dependent, MUR 20,000 each for up to 3 more
Not where the employer pays, nor under a combined medical and life scheme
The contribution or MUR 50,000, whichever is lower
A scheme approved by the Financial Services Commission
The amount or MUR 100,000, whichever is lower
The wages or MUR 30,000, whichever is lower

blocks.text: The deduction for household employees' wages ended on 30 June 2025, with the reliefs for adopting animals and for angel investors.

sections.heading: What comes off a salary: PAYE, CSG and the National Savings Fund

blocks.text: Under Pay As You Earn (PAYE) the employer withholds income tax from each month's pay, on a cumulative sum over the income year. An employee claims deductions on an Employee Declaration Form. One thirteenth of them is counted each month, the end of year bonus being the thirteenth. No tax is withheld where a month's emoluments are MUR 38,462 or less. Without a form, tax is withheld at a flat 15%, or 20% if the employee asks.

rows: CSG, monthly basic pay of MUR 50,000 or less
The whole basic wage or salary
CSG, monthly basic pay above MUR 50,000
The whole basic wage or salary
Basic pay up to MUR 29,710 a month, from 1 July 2026. None under MUR 4,580 a month

items: Basic pay leaves out overtime, bonuses and allowances. For CSG, an end of year bonus counts as a month of its own.
The employer pays its own share on top: 3% or 6% for CSG and 2.5% for the National Savings Fund.

blocks.text: A self-employed person pays on the same bands, on the profit of the business with any other income, less the same deductions. Under the Current Payment System (CPS) a quarterly statement and payment are due where last year's gross income from business and rent was above MUR 4 million. The quarters to September, December and March are due 2 days before the end of December, on 31 March and 2 days before the end of June, not counting Saturdays and public holidays. The rest is paid with the yearly return.

rows: 1.5% of 90% of net income, and never less than MUR 150

items: A month's net income can be taken as one twelfth of last year's. A yearly CSG return, paid in advance, is due by 15 October.
A small business in farming, manufacturing, retail or wholesale may choose a presumptive tax instead: see our guide to business taxes.

sections.heading: The return and when it is due

items: A return is due from anyone with net income above MUR 500,000, business gross income above MUR 2 million, tax withheld under PAYE or deducted at source, or a chargeable income. Other self-employed people file a simplified return.
It is filed, and any tax paid, electronically by 15 October. For the year ended 30 June 2026 that was Thursday 15 October 2026.
A late return costs MUR 2,000 a month, up to MUR 5,000 for an individual not in business. Tax paid late bears a penalty of 2.5%, or 1% for such an individual, and interest of 0.25% a month.

unverified: An MRA circular or PAYE table for the income year 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. On 20 November 2026 the MRA's PAYE page, its page on the obligation to file and its tax calculator still showed the bands for 2025-2026, with no 35% band. The bands here are from the Finance Act 2026 and the Income Tax Act as consolidated up to it.
How an employer withholds the 35% band month by month. The cumulative method is set by regulations, which were not read for 2026-2027.

Whether the MRA allows the additional deduction of MUR 50,000 for a retired or disabled person in the same way in 2026-2027. The amount is in section 27(2A) of the Act as consolidated. The MRA's page for the year defines a retired person and a disabled person but gives no amount.

The rate at which tax is charged on a quarterly CPS statement. Section 108 of the Act leaves it to regulations. The MRA's self-employed page gives 15%, but that page also shows penalty rates that were replaced on 1 July 2025.
The age at which National Savings Fund contributions stop. The MRA page gives 65 for pay periods from August 2018. It was not checked against later changes to pension law.
How the deduction for private school fees is shared where both parents pay fees. The Act and the MRA page give the cap for each child and say no more.
